fhb-share.html: In September 2026, New Zealand banks approved 2,667 first-home buyer mortgages totalling $1.53B—accounting for 20.3% of all new residential mortgage lending (up from 19.2% a year earlier), with an average loan size of $573,678.

fhb-share.source_html:
HLF calculation: $1,530m ÷ $7,533m = 20.3% (Mean loan: $1,530m × $1m ÷ 2,667 = $573,678; RBNZ dollar series rounded to $1m)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31) • Direct RBNZ C31 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 14 November 2026.

Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33) • Direct RBNZ C33 .xlsx • Glossary: Refinancing · Usable Equity • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 14 November 2026.

top-ups.html: In September 2026, 9,639 homeowners were approved for a mortgage top-up on their existing property—accounting for 46.4% of all mortgage approvals across New Zealand, with an average top-up of $99,803.
top-ups.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C33 (September 2026): Top-up approvals = 9,639 borrowers ($962m) out of 20,763 total approvals.
top-ups.source_html:

Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33) • Direct RBNZ C33 .xlsx • Glossary: Refinancing · Usable Equity • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 14 November 2026.

top-ups.source_full: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by purpose (Table C33)
top-ups.data_type: Officially reported RBNZ series & HLF-derived share/mean
top-ups.definition: The percentage of all monthly residential mortgage approvals that are top-ups on an existing mortgage with the same lender, alongside the mean dollar top-up size.
top-ups.formula: (Top-up Count [LVRN.MMB2.AZB] ÷ Total Approvals by Purpose) × 100; Mean Top-Up = LVRN.MMB1.AZB ÷ LVRN.MMB2.AZB
top-ups.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Top-ups are one of the most common transactions in New Zealand banking—used by homeowners to fund renovations, deposits on investment properties, or major capital purchases.
top-ups.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C33 by dividing top-up borrower count (LVRN.MMB2.AZB) by total mortgage approvals across all purposes, and dividing top-up lending value (LVRN.MMB1.AZB, rounded to $1m) by top-up borrower count.

dti-headroom.formula: (FHB Lending with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB Commitments across all TDTI bands) × 100; Headroom = 20.0% minus (>6x Share)

HLF calculation: ($850m × $1m ÷ 1,342 = $633,383) minus ($680m × $1m ÷ 1,325 = $513,208) = $120,175 (subject to RBNZ $1m rounding)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — New residential mortgage lending by borrower type (Table C31) • Direct RBNZ C31 .xlsx • Glossary: Loan-to-Value Ratio (LVR) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 14 November 2026.

borrower-income.formula: Sum(Band Total Gross Income [$m]) ÷ Sum(Band Total Gross Income [$m] ÷ Band Average Gross Income [$k]) × 1,000 (subject to RBNZ $0.1m / $1,000 band rounding)
borrower-income.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: RBNZ's Borrower Gross Income (BGI) measures total application income (which for couples combines two salaries, and for investors includes existing salaries plus gross rental and other qualifying income).

fhb-dti-headroom.html: In September 2026, 9.1% of first-home buyer mortgage lending had a Debt-to-Income (DTI) ratio above 6x ($139.0m of $1,527.0m)—sitting 10.9 percentage points below the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap.
fhb-dti-headroom.official_data_summary: RBNZ Table C40 (September 2026): FHB lending with TDTI > 6 = $139.0m out of $1,527.0m total FHB commitments.
fhb-dti-headroom.source_html:
HLF calculation: $139.0m ÷ $1,527.0m = 9.1% (Benchmark diff: 20.0% - 9.1% = 10.9 pts)
Source: Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Residential mortgage lending by Debt-to-Income (DTI) purpose use (Table C40) • Direct RBNZ C40 .xlsx • Glossary: Debt-to-Income (DTI) • Derived by HLF Pulse (CC BY 4.0) • Checked: 14 November 2026.

fhb-dti-headroom.definition: The percentage of total monthly first-home buyer mortgage lending value committed at a Total Debt-to-Income (TDTI) ratio above 6x gross income, compared against the 20% RBNZ speed-limit cap on non-exempt owner-occupier lending.
fhb-dti-headroom.formula: (FHB Lending with TDTI > 6 ÷ Total FHB Commitments across all TDTI bands) × 100; Headroom = 20.0% minus (>6x Share)
fhb-dti-headroom.hlf_interpretation: HLF market context: Because bank test servicing rates already constrain borrowing capacity, total FHB lending above 6x DTI sits well inside the 20% RBNZ speed-limit allowance.
fhb-dti-headroom.methodology: Derived from RBNZ Table C40 by summing first-home buyer lending commitments in bands above 6x TDTI (including unknown TDTI) and dividing by total first-home buyer commitments across all TDTI bands.
